content_metadata.description: A video clip showing the struggle of children to survive in a hostile world where they are left to fend for themselves.

scenes.contextualRelevance: The text implies that the kids have been trapped for a long time and have been fighting amongst themselves, suggesting a breakdown of social order.

mood.description: Pensive - The use of text against a black screen sets a serious and introspective tone.

keyMoments.changeDescription: The text implies that the kids have been trapped for a long time and have been fighting amongst themselves, suggesting a breakdown of social order.

narrativeProgression.description: Setting the stage for the conflict – the kids are trapped, resources are scarce, and nature itself has become hostile.

videoEditingDetails.description: Black screen with white text providing a brief synopsis of the series

activities.description: School bus driving through a field of cabbages
Children exiting the bus and looking around

scenes.contextualRelevance: The dilapidated state of the school bus suggests a world where things have fallen apart. The children’s clothing is worn and dirty, further emphasizing a lack of resources.

mood.description: Anxious - The wide shots of the field create a sense of isolation, while the children’s expressions convey apprehension about their surroundings.

keyMoments.changeDescription: Shift from a calm visual (driving through the field) to a more anxious one as Albert exits the bus with a tense expression.

narrativeProgression.description: Introducing the setting (the cabbage field) and hinting at the growing tension among the group.
A school bus full of children arrives at a cabbage field, suggesting this is their source of food.
Astrid comments on the cabbages, implying they may be their only option for sustenance.
The children gather near the bus, apprehensive and unsure of what to do.

scenes.thematicElements: Scarcity of resources, the burden of leadership, uncertainty.

videoEditingDetails.description: Wide shot of a field of cabbages.
The camera zooms in on the front of the bus, specifically on Albert getting out of the driver’s seat.
The camera follows Albert as he gets out of the bus and scans the field.

activities.description: Albert explaining the situation and plan to children

characterInteraction.description: Albert takes charge, trying to motivate the group.
Quinn expresses doubt, while Sam remains silent and observant.
Howard seems resigned to their fate.

scenes.contextualRelevance: The children’s reaction to Albert’s suggestion of eating cabbages underscores their loss of innocence and their struggle to adapt to a world without the comforts they once had.

mood.description: Anxious - Albert’s blunt words about the lack of food heighten the sense of desperation. Quinn’s nervousness and Howard’s resignation further contribute to the overall tension.

keyMoments.changeDescription: Albert reveals that they have run out of all other food options, emphasizing their desperate situation.
Quinn questions the logic of eating cabbages, highlighting the absurdity of their current reality.
Albert urges the group to start gathering food, setting the scene for potential danger.

narrativeProgression.description: Establishing the dire circumstances and the necessity of finding food.

scenes.thematicElements: Hunger, survival instincts, acceptance of harsh realities.

videoEditingDetails.description: Medium shot of Albert addressing the other kids.
Quick series of cuts between characters reflects tension.
Wide shot of the children running toward the cabbage field.

activities.description: Howard tries to convince Albert to be more understanding
The children discover something is wrong in the field
Quinn getting eaten by cabbage monster and bleeding out

characterInteraction.description: Howard confronts Albert about his leadership style.
The children’s shared terror briefly unites them as they flee for their lives.

scenes.contextualRelevance: Quinn, who initially dismissed the idea of eating cabbages, becomes the victim of the very thing he doubted. This serves as a harsh reminder that their situation is no longer a game.

mood.description: Involving several emotions shifting from Angry -> Anxious -> Terrified.

keyMoments.changeDescription: Shift from tense dialogue to a mounting sense of unease as the children search for food.
Abrupt shift from visual calm to intense terror as the creature appears and the children flee.
Eerie silence after the children reach the bus, broken only by Albert’s panicked calls for Quinn.
A horrifying visual and distorted audio as Quinn is attacked, creating a sense of dread and despair.

narrativeProgression.description: The danger foreshadowed in the previous scenes comes to a head, leaving the characters traumatized.

scenes.thematicElements: Loss of innocence, the fragility of life, the consequences of desperation.

videoEditingDetails.description: Close-up shot of Howard talking to Albert.
Wide shot of the children walking through the field.
Close-up on Sam as he notices movement in the field.
The camera follows the children as they run back to the bus in a panic.
Close-up on Albert as he searches for Quinn.
Long shot of Quinn trying to escape, then attacked by the cabbage monster.

scenes.contextualRelevance: The logo fading out into darkness symbolizes the loss of hope and the bleak future facing the surviving children.

mood.description: Sad - The sudden silence and the return to the black screen, coupled with the knowledge of Quinn’s fate, create a heavy and somber atmosphere.

narrativeProgression.description: A moment of reflection on the events that have just transpired.

scenes.thematicElements: Mortality, grief, the lingering impact of trauma.

videoEditingDetails.description: Black screen with the “Gone” logo fading in and out.

climax.description: The climax occurs when Quinn is attacked and killed by the cabbage monster, demonstrating the unforgiving nature of their new reality.

storylines.description: The entire clip focuses on the struggle of the children to survive in a world where they have been left to fend for themselves.

The bus ride sequence could be trimmed slightly. A shorter shot of the bus approaching the field would suffice.
Howard and Albert's conversation could be shortened to keep the focus on the escalating tension.

youtube_description:
A teaser scene from book two of #MichaelGrant's New York Times bestselling #GONE series, for a potential #TV adaptation.

One day, without warning or explanation, every person over the age of 16 disappears from the town of Perdido Beach, California. No parents, no teachers, no cops, no doctors. No explanation. 332 kids remain, from age 16 down to babies in their cribs. They are trapped in a world without authority, a chaotic, deadly world where some kids are developing superpowers and some of those with superpowers are very dangerous.

Be a part of bringing GONE: The TV Series to life — follow our Twitter and Instagram accounts!
https://twitter.com/GoneTheSeries
https://instagram.com/GoneTheSeries

And follow Michael Grant on Twitter: https://twitter.com/MichaelGrantBks

We originally shot this in November 2019 and finished post-production in the middle of the pandemic. Now, it's ready to share with the world.
